'''Linda Preiss Rothschild''' ({{nee}} Preiss; born February 28, 1945) is a [[professor emeritus]] of mathematics at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.ucsd.edu/~lrothsch/cv.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved January 1, 2015.</ref> Her thesis research concerned [[Lie group]]s, but subsequently her interests broadened to include also [[polynomial factorization]], [[partial differential equation]]s, [[harmonic analysis]], and the theory of [[several complex variables]].<ref name="noether">{{citation|url=http://www.awm-math.org/noetherbrochure/Rothschild97.html|title=Linda Preiss Rothschild|website=Profiles of Women in Mathematics|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|accessdate=January 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307210958/http://www.awm-math.org/noetherbrochure/Rothschild97.html|archive-date=March 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

== Education and career ==
The daughter of Philadelphia fur merchants, she was unable to attend the best high school of the city, which were then  restricted to boys. She graduated from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1966.<ref name="cv" /><ref name="noether" /> Rejected from graduate study at [[Princeton University]] because it was also male-only,<ref name="noether" /><ref name="bwm">{{citation|url=http://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/rothschild.htm|title=Linda Preiss Rothschild|website=Biographies of Women Mathematicians|first=Larry|last=Riddle|publisher=[[Agnes Scott College]]|date=2014|accessdate=January 1, 2015}}</ref> she  earned her Ph.D. in 1970 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under the supervision of [[Isadore Singer]].<ref name="cv" /><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=31661}}</ref>

She held temporary positions at MIT, [[Tufts University]], [[Columbia University]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], and [[Princeton University]] before landing an associate professorship at the [[University of Wisconsin]] in 1976. She moved to San Diego in 1983,<ref name="cv" /><ref name="noether" /> and retired in 2011.<ref name="bwm" />

Rothschild was a Member at Large at the [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] from 1977 to 1979.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en |archive-date=March 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306081906/https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> She served as president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] from 1983 to 1985, and vice president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] from 1985 to 1987. She has been co-editor-in-chief of the journal ''Mathematical Research Letters'' since 1994.<ref name="cv" /><ref name="bwm" />

The mother of two sons by her first marriage, her 
second husband, [[M. Salah Baouendi]], was a distinguished professor of mathematics at UC San Diego; he died in 2011.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/nytimes/obituary.aspx?pid=155534170|newspaper=[[New York Times]]|title=Death Notice: M. Salah Baouendi (1937–2011)|date=January 1, 2015}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Rothschild was awarded a [[Sloan Fellowship]] in 1976.<ref name="cv" /><ref name="noether" />
In 1997, Rothschild gave the [[Noether Lecture]] of the Association for Women in Mathematics, on the subject "How do Real Manifolds live in Complex Space?",<ref name="cv" /><ref name="noether" /> and she was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2006.<ref name="bwm" /> She was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2005,<ref name="bwm" /> and in 2012 she became one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|accessdate=January 1, 2015|archive-date=August 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref> A conference in her honor was held in 2008 at the [[University of Fribourg]] in Switzerland.<ref name="bwm" /> In 2017, she was selected as a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 Inaugural Class of AWM Fellows|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2018-awm-fellows|website=awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=January 9, 2021}}</ref>

She and her husband were jointly awarded the [[Stefan Bergman#The Bergman Prize|Stefan Bergman Prize]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2003.<ref name="bwm" />
